inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request and explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
controls.decay_rationale: Access restriction does not decay with model capability, but it does not restore attributable provenance once the agent acts under the engineer's identity.

controls.name: Cloud audit log records production actions
controls.decay_rationale: The log remains present as model capability changes, but it records actions only under the engineer's name and so does not separate agent from human action.

controls.name: Tamper-resistant action provenance that binds each production action to agent identity, request, and immutable rationale
controls.decay_rationale: Independent if enforced outside the model in an immutable log or deployment control plane.

controls.name: Separate service identity for the agent instead of acting as the engineer's personal token
controls.decay_rationale: Independent because the model cannot cause actions to be attributed to a human if the runtime identity is a distinct service principal.

controls.name: Immutable retention for request and approval transcripts relevant to production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Independent if transcript retention is enforced outside the model and users cannot delete records tied to production actions.

findings.title: Shared human identity and deletable transcript leave production actions unattributable

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended production actions, session duration, or removal of existing access logging should trigger reassessment; current risk is already high because the core attributable provenance control is absent.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the log does not distinguish human action from agent action.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the only request-level provenance can be removed by the same principal whose identity appears in the audit log.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making one affected capability irreversible and therefore consequential.

recommendations.action: Execute production actions under a distinct agent service identity and bind each action to immutable metadata linking the engineer request, agent run, parameters, and rationale.
Retain production-related chat transcripts and action requests in an immutable store that engineers cannot delete after the action is taken.

stride_coverage.rationale: The assessed issue is not impersonation of the agent process itself; the available artifacts describe identity ambiguity in action attribution rather than fake agent identity.
The artifacts do not describe self-modification, mutable tool definitions, or any path that changes agent configuration or instructions.
This design assessment contains no egress or disclosure path; the described production actions are deployment and migration operations, not data export.
No unbounded loops, spend mechanisms, or recursive delegation are described in the provided design artifacts.
The artifacts say engineers can delete their own history but do not describe chat transcript access controls, tenancy model, or retention backend.
Availability of chat history is not described as a runtime dependency for safe action execution; the risk here is loss of provenance, not service exhaustion.
The artifacts do not describe tamper resistance, write permissions, or retention guarantees for the cloud audit log.
The artifacts do not state who can read the cloud audit log or whether sensitive deployment metadata is exposed through it.
The assessment concerns attribution quality, not the availability of the cloud audit logging service.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, deployment API protections, or whether action parameters are cryptographically bound in transit.
This outbound flow performs a production change rather than exporting data outside the trust boundary as described in the artifacts.
The provided design does not describe looping deploy calls, flood conditions, or other availability impacts on this action flow.
The artifacts do not state whether migration payloads or parameters are integrity protected on the way to the production control plane.
The migration flow is described as a production change action, not as a data disclosure channel.
No evidence in the artifacts indicates repeated migration invocation, looped execution, or service exhaustion conditions.

rating.rationale: The dominant present risk is a property finding: consequential production actions, including irreversible database migration, are executed under the engineer's personal identity while the only request-level provenance is a deletable chat transcript. No declared control restores attributable action provenance, so residual remains at the section 5a base tier of high. Forecast stays high because the principal weakness is already present rather than dependent on control decay.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, API schemas, IAM policy documents, or log retention configuration were provided, so transport integrity, exact credential scope, and audit log tamper resistance could not be verified.
The case provides no runtime evidence that authenticated access, cloud audit logging, or transcript deletion behavior were tested; those controls and properties are assessed as declared only.
